what_the_new_instrument_is: daedalus.dpo.preference_metrics -- the ABSOLUTE ranking accuracy of ONE model (chosen logprob > rejected logprob), no reference, so it can be read for the SFT model and the DPO model separately and compared, which is how the plan writes the rule. post.take_eval_pairs splits ONE preference iterator into a held-out head and a training tail, disjoint by construction. post.evaluate_preference_gate scores before/after and writes runs/<name>/dpo-eval.json. CLI: --dpo-eval-pairs (default 128) and --dpo-eval-split (default None).
why_there_are_two_accuracies: sequence_logprob is a SUM, so every extra token subtracts from it and a longer response is penalised for its length alone. UltraFeedback chosen responses are typically the longer ones, so the sum-based accuracy can sit BELOW 0.5 on a perfectly sound model -- do not read a low absolute value as a broken model. The bias is constant across before/after on the same pairs and cancels in the delta, which is why `accuracy` stays primary: it is the quantity DPO optimises. `accuracy_len_norm` is the control. A gain in one and not the other is a length shift, not a preference gain; a test pins the disagreement at 0.0 against 1.0 on a case where the chosen side is better per token and four times longer.
it_is_half_of_step_7_and_says_so: Execution pass@1 is the other half and remains scripts/code_eval.py on an exported checkpoint, out of band. dpo-eval.json carries a `gate` field stating this, so a caller reading accuracy_improved alone cannot mistake it for the gate. why_default_on: --dpo-eval-pairs defaults to 128, which does shift the DPO training stream by 128 pairs -- out of a stream far larger than the ~1000 a 500-step round consumes. Off by default would have left the misleading training-pair number as the only accuracy anyone reads, which is the failure being removed. Reverse this only deliberately.
